A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the game model and the post-optimally analyses of the energy consumption model are very useful for decision making in energy utilities, especially for the determination of break-even points for the consumers, and thus, the need for a dual tariff policy in residential and workplace buildings.

the post-optimization analysis of energy consumption model and utility application provides a useful tool that can be applied for decision making purposes in residential energy consumption and distribution, especially for Utilities.

the mixed strategy of optimal energy consumption game values obtained from the game models for winter and summer residential seasons can be considered as an alternative tool for the usual statistical analysis of minimum and maximum values of energy consumption.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the post-optimally analysis of the game model provides an extended and flexible range of energy values for utilities, and thus, it provides a useful tool in the decision making process for the energy utilities and consumers.

the energy consumption model is not only a useful tool for utilities and decision makers but also for consumers to understand the energy consumption patterns and to make informed decisions on their energy use and consumption.

it provides a useful tool to Utilities for identifying flexibility range in the optimal break-even energy value for consumers in the informal settlements, where metering is a challenge and thus a uniform tariff is used for all.
